subject: biology
title: Heart & Vessels
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet your heart's four chambers and the three types of blood vessel.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology circulatory system — heart chambers, valves, double circulation, arteries veins capillaries.
final_note: You learned the heart chambers and valves, double circulation, and what makes each vessel type special.

concepts.def: Upper heart chamber that receives blood from veins
Lower heart chamber that pumps blood out
Two loops — heart to lungs, heart to body
Thick muscular vessel carrying blood away from heart
Thinner vessel with valves bringing blood back

walkthroughs.body_html:
Your heart has two sides with two chambers each.

Right atrium and right ventricle handle deoxygenated blood.

Left atrium and left ventricle handle oxygenated blood. Valves (tricuspid right, bicuspid left, plus semilunar) stop backflow.

Blood goes around twice per circuit — this is double circulation.

Loop 1 (pulmonary): right heart → lungs → left heart. Blood picks up oxygen.

Loop 2 (systemic): left heart → body → right heart. Blood drops oxygen at cells. The left ventricle has the thickest wall — it pumps furthest.

Arteries: thick muscular walls — handle high pressure leaving the heart.

Veins: thinner walls but have valves — low-pressure return to the heart.

Capillaries: just one cell thick — perfect for swapping oxygen, glucose and CO₂ with body cells.

mcqs.q: Which heart chamber pumps oxygenated blood out to the body?
options: Right atrium
Right ventricle
Left atrium
Left ventricle

mcqs.q: Which blood vessel has walls just ONE cell thick?
options: Artery
Vein
Capillary
Aorta

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
Neurones touch each other at synapses and pass current through direct contact.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.

mcqs.q: How are signals transmitted across a synapse between two neurones?
options: Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
Via neurotransmitter chemicals released from the presynaptic neurone, which bind receptors on the postsynaptic neurone.
Neurones touch each other at synapses and pass current through direct contact.
The electrical signal jumps directly from one neurone to the next across the synaptic gap.

mcqs.q: Why is a reflex action faster than a conscious response?
options: The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
The signal does not need to be processed by the brain — it travels through a simpler reflex arc via the spinal cord.
The brain decides reflexes faster than other actions because it skips thinking.

mcqs.q: How many chambers does a human heart have in total?
Blood leaves the left ventricle and travels to the body. Which vessel does it enter first?
options: The aorta
The pulmonary artery
The vena cava
The pulmonary vein

mcqs.q: Veins contain valves but arteries (other than at the heart) do not. What is the main reason?
options: Blood in veins is at low pressure and valves stop backflow.
Veins carry blood away from the heart at high pressure.
Valves help arteries stretch with each heartbeat.
Veins carry only oxygenated blood.

mcqs.q: Red blood cells have no nucleus and are biconcave. How does this adapt them to their function?
options: More room and surface area for carrying oxygen
They can divide rapidly to make more cells
They can engulf pathogens more easily
They can photosynthesise in the blood

mcqs.q: In which type of vessel does the exchange of oxygen, glucose and waste with body cells actually take place?
options: Capillaries
Arteries
Veins
The aorta

sequence.def: Receives deoxygenated blood from the vena cava
Pumps blood to the lungs via the pulmonary artery
Blood is oxygenated and CO2 removed
Receives oxygenated blood via the pulmonary vein
Pumps oxygenated blood out via the aorta
Oxygenated blood delivered to the whole body
